Supplying ``volume`` lists that volume's books. Omitting ``volume`` runs a

Query a resource's tabular data with PostgREST-style filters.

The output format is negotiated via the ``Accept`` header:
``application/json`` (default, a JSON array of row objects), ``text/csv``,
or ``application/parquet``.

Column filters use a dynamic ``col.op=value`` grammar that cannot be
enumerated in a static schema because the columns are per-resource, so they
arrive as arbitrary query params alongside the four declared modifiers.
Operators: ``eq`` (the default when ``.op`` is omitted), ``neq``, ``gt``,
``gte``, ``lt``, ``lte``, ``in``, ``nin``, ``like``, ``ilike``, ``is``,
``isnot`` — e.g. ``?year.gte=2020&region.in=USA,CHN``.

Returns 304 when ``If-None-Match`` matches the computed ETag for published,
non-invalidated resources.

post.description:
Attach a resource to a draft book by tracking id.

Re-points a resource owned by another DRAFT book (409 only when the current
owner is PUBLISHED); asserts WRITE access to the source draft's volume and
emits a ``BOOK_ATTACH`` audit event on every move.

get.description:
List a book's entries (read-only, cursor-paginated).

Visibility-aware like the other v1 book reads: a book the caller cannot
see resolves to 404 (never 403), and entries are filtered by the book's
visibility tier. Works for drafts and published books alike, so producers
can inspect a draft's membership without publishing it.

get.description:
List a book's lifecycle events (read-only, cursor-paginated).

Visibility-aware like the other v1 book reads: a book the caller cannot
see resolves to 404 (never 403). Returns the book's publish / invalidate
events plus the attach events that moved a resource into or out of it.
Attach events whose cross-referenced sibling book or moved resource the
caller cannot see are omitted, so a hidden sibling/resource/user is never
leaked through a visible book's history.

Register a homogeneous list of resources.

With ``atomic=True`` (default), all items succeed or none do — any
per-item failure rolls the whole transaction back and surfaces the
failing item's real status (e.g. **409** for a conflict) with a curated
``Problem`` body carrying ``failed_index``.

With ``atomic=False``, items are processed independently; failures
surface in the per-item ``error`` field while siblings continue.

External pointers are detected from ``item.external_uri``; no separate
endpoint is required.

The Activity envelope, when supplied, is persisted lazily — if
``items`` is empty, no Activity row is written.

Offline-flush replay with per-item status reporting.

Items are processed independently — one item failing does not stop the
others.  The response status is always 200; callers inspect each
``BulkItemResult`` for individual outcomes.

ChartVisibility.title: ChartVisibility
ChartVisibility.description:
Visibility for Data Explorer charts.

Distinct from :class:`Visibility` (resources/books) because explorer charts
are shared by unguessable ``short_id`` link, so they need an ``unlisted``
tier rather than ``hidden``:

- ``public`` — listed in discovery and readable by anyone with the link.
- ``unlisted`` — not listed, but still readable by anyone with the link
  (including anonymous callers).
- ``private`` — readable only by the owner and members of the owner's org;
  everyone else (including anonymous) gets a 404.

Default is ``public`` to preserve the pre-privacy behaviour of saved charts.

DiscoveryProfile.title: DiscoveryProfile
DiscoveryProfile.description:
Typed discovery and release metadata for a volume.

This is the consumer-facing profile the catalogue reads.
It answers what the dataset is, what it covers, how current it is
and whether it is still fit to use,
without clients having to interpret arbitrary keys in ``metadata``.
Field names follow DCAT and DataCite concepts where they line up.
Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored, so a caller who misspells a
field, or sends one the profile deliberately does not carry, hears about it
instead of silently losing the value.

dedupe.description: When ``True`` (default) the server checks whether a resource with the same content hash already exists and returns an ``aliased`` outcome if so. Set to ``False`` for per-book entry resources (notebooks, outputs) so that each edition owns a distinct resource row even when the bytes are identical.

RegisterResourceItem.title: RegisterResourceItem
RegisterResourceItem.description:
One resource registration in a homogeneous list.

A single item type covers both managed and external-pointer flows.
When ``external_uri`` is set the registration is treated as J3 (external
pointer); otherwise it is a managed (S3-backed) registration.

status.title: Status
status.description: ``created`` / ``merged`` / ``aliased`` on success, ``error`` when the item failed under ``atomic=False`` semantics.

activity.description: Optional Activity envelope. Persisted lazily — if ``items`` is empty, no Activity row is written.

atomic.title: Atomic
atomic.description: True for strict-atomic semantics; False to allow per-item failures.

RegisterResourcesRequest.title: RegisterResourcesRequest
RegisterResourcesRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /v1/resources/registrations``.

Unions the legacy single + batch shapes: a homogeneous list of items
(every item is either managed or external, indicated by
``item.external_uri``), an optional ``Activity`` envelope, and an
``atomic`` flag.

* ``atomic=True`` (default): strict transaction — any failure rolls back
  the whole batch and surfaces 422 with ``failed_index``.
* ``atomic=False``: per-item processing — failures are reported in line
  while siblings continue.

activity_created.title: Activity Created
activity_created.description: True when the Activity envelope was persisted in this call. False on lazy no-op or idempotent replay.

activity_id.title: Activity Id
activity_id.description: Activity id when an envelope was supplied or matched an existing row. ``null`` when no activity was supplied AND items is empty.

atomic.title: Atomic
atomic.description: Echo of the request's atomic flag.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Event payload. Internal bookkeeping keys recording the acting org/admin are stripped for non-admin and anonymous callers; admins receive the full payload.
